parties:
Haji Md. Ishaque and others ------ Appellants.
Vs.
Rupali Bank------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff appellants filed Other Suit No.32 of 1986 in the said Court against the principal defendant respondent No.1, Rupali Bank and other proforma respondents for declaring the ex-parte preliminary decree dated 16.1.1986 and final decree dated 2.6.1986 passed in the said suit as illegal, fraudulent and collusive. 

 3. The case of the plaintiff appellants, inter alia, is that the defendants Nos. 7-9 mortgaged the suit property to the then Standard Bank on 25.8.1969 as security to the loan of Tk. 1,1,65,000/- incurred by them and their partners for carrying on their business under the name of defendant No.2, M/S. Sunrise Tea House; that subsequently the Standard Bank was amalgamated with the defendant No.1, Rupali Bank; that the plaintiffs purchased the suit property from the defendants Nos. 7, 8, 10 and 11 by 8 sale deeds dated 10.6.77, 5.9.77 and 6.9.77 and are in possession thereof from the date of agreement for sale in part performance of the contract; that a portion of the suit property is in possession of the defendant Bank as monthly tenant; that the plaintiffs came to know on 12.1.86, that the defendant No.1, Rupali Bank, obtained an ex-parte decree on 16.1.86, in Mortgage Suit No.32 of 1974, without serving notice upon the defendants of that suit; that the plaintiffs were not impleaded as defendants in that suit; that the claimed amount in the suit was repaid and the same was suppressed from the Court and a fraudulent ex-parte decree was obtained. 

 6. Mr. Mozammel Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant submitted that there was no admission in the plaint that the defendant No.1 is in possession of the suit property but there is a statement to the effect that the defendant No.1 has been possessing a portion of the suit property as monthly tenant and possession of a monthly tenant is the possession of the landlord plaintiffs and as such the plaintiffs were not required to pay for recovery of possession on payment of advalorem court fee in suit for declaring a fraudulent ex-parte decree as void. He further submitted that the Court below was wholly wrong to reject the plaint without giving a chance to the plaintiffs to pay advalorem court fee and only on the failure of the plaintiffs to comply with any such direction from the Court the plaint could be rejected. He further submitted that the purchases by the plaintiffs during the pendency of mortgage suit are subject to the result of the suit but the said purchases of the said property are not void and the plaintiffs have locus standi to file the suit to protect their interest in the suit property. He further submitted that the claim of the plaintiffs in the earlier suit being false the ex-parte decree obtained on the basis of such false claim is fraudulent. 

 7. Mr. Syed Moazzem Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.1, submitted that falsity of the claim in the suit cannot be a ground for setting aside ex-parte decree on the ground of fraud unless the plaintiffs succeeds in showing that by the fraudulent suppression of the summons upon them in the earlier suit they were prevented from contesting the false claim of the plaintiffs of the earlier suit. He submitted that the plaintiffs in the four corners of their plaint did not allege fraudulent suppression of summons on the defendants of that suit they rather alleged that they purchased the suit property during pendency of the earlier suit and they were not impleaded in that suit. In support of his contention he referred to the case of Chapala Sundari Devi Vs. Wahed Ali and others, reported in 11 D.L.R. 376. He further submitted that the plaintiffs purchased admittedly during the pendency of the earlier suit the same were hit by doctrine of Lis pendense under Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, and the plaintiffs having not impleaded themselves in the earlier suit with leave of the Court as assignees of the owner defendants the decree passed against their vendors cannot he challenged by the plaintiffs. The learned Advocate found it difficult to support the other reason given by the Court below for rejecting the plain for not praying for recovery of possession on payment of advalorem court fee. 

 9. The plaintiffs admittedly purchased the suit property in 1977 by 8 sale deeds during pendency of mortgage suit No.32 of 1974 for recovery of Tk. 3,22,636.20 and they alleged that the sum of Tk. 2,59,936.00 was paid during the pendency of the suit. On 8.9.76 and 8.9.79. Even if the contention of the plaintiffs are accepted to be true, it cannot be said that the claim of the plaintiffs of the said suit was false and as much the impugned ex-parte decree passed in the suit was not fraudulent. Any payment during the pendency of the suit to the plaintiffs without any order from the Court cannot be adjusted against the claim in the suit. Under the provision of Order XXIII Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure if the defendant can satisfy the Court that the claim in the suit has been adjusted or satisfied wholly or in part by any lawful agreement or compromise then the Court shall pass a decree in terms of such compromise. But nowhere in the plaint it has been stated that the defendants of that suit paid the sum of Tk. 2,59,936.00 to the defendant No.1 Bank in terms of any compromise and that no attempt was made by the defendants in that suit to record such compromise. In such circumstances it cannot be said that the claim of the defendant No.1 in the said Mortgage suit for recovery of Tk. 3,22,636.20 was false for not adjusting the same sum of Tk. 2,59,936. 00 from the claim. 

 10. It is settled law that falsity of a claim cannot be a ground for setting aside an ex-parte decree. Only when the plaintiff challenges an ex-parte decree on the ground of fraudulent suppression of summons to deprive him from the opportunity of contesting the false claim in such a suit the plaintiff can establish such allegation of fraudulent suppression of summons then such an ex-parte decree can be set aside as fraudulent. In this case there is no allegation of fraudulent suppression of summons on the defendants and as such on the ground of falsity of the claim the impugned ex-parte decree cannot be set aside or declared illegal. 

 11. The Court below found that on the basis of the transfer deeds from the proforma defendants the plaintiffs of the present suit have no locus standi to bring the suit. Admittedly the plaintiffs purchased the suit property during the pendency of the mortgage suit and they having not got themselves impleaded in that suit as assignee of their vendor defendants under the provision of Order XXII Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure and contested the claim of the defendant No.1 who was plaintiff in the mortgage suit, the impugned decree is binding on the plaintiff appellants. As such the plaintiff appellants cannot challenge the impugned decree. We, therefore, hold that the plaintiffs have no cause of action for the suit and the Court below rightly rejected the plaint.
